embeds.title: 🔴 Microsoft Patches Critical Zero-Click Outlook Vulnerability CVE-2026-40361
embeds.description:
Microsoft patched CVE-2026-40361, a critical zero-click remote code execution vulnerability in Outlook's email rendering engine affecting Word and Outlook. Researcher Haifei Li, who developed the zero-day detection system Expmon, reported the vulnerability. The flaw is a use-after-free bug that can be exploited when victims read or preview emails without clicking links or attachments. Li compared it to CVE-2015-6172 (BadWinmail), noting both have the same attack vector and potential to compromise executives by sending malicious emails that bypass enterprise firewalls. Microsoft assigned it an 'exploitation more likely' rating. Li developed only a proof-of-concept rather than a working exploit.
**Sources:** SecurityWeek • 🔴 1 corroborating
